scope: Different-author, read-only source hammer of the sealed M1832 C2 fresh-mapped two-axis Formality and dual-corner PrimeTime source package. The review recomputed source and authority seals, inspected the exact 13-row RTL/filelist and both axes' mapped Verilog/SDC/SVF pins, checked the two-Formality/two-PrimeTime execution shape, slow-max/fast-min OCV setup/hold reporting and claim boundary, and attacked live-source drift and release-authority separation. No EDA, simulator, license query, attempt, result, release, canonical write, predecessor write, docs359 write, commit or push was performed.
verdict: FAIL CLOSED. The intended two-axis Formality/PT flow is structurally sound, uses distinct K8 ARCH_MODE=0 and K1x8 ARCH_MODE=1 artifacts, and preserves negative timing slack. However, launch-time authority does not exact-pin the 13 live RTL source contents consumed by fresh Formality, and the future M1836 release is structurally unable to pin the M1834 review manifest and outer seal. These are two P1 authorization/identity blockers. PT report completeness and semantic coverage checking remains a P2 result-hammer requirement. M1834 authorizes zero attempts and zero EDA runs.

findings.title: Fresh Formality consumes 13 live RTL files without launch-time exact-content verification
findings.evidence: verify_authority() exact-pins only the filelist text and checks that it has 13 unique rows. It does not call exact_regular() on the 13 resolved RTL files or compare them with the exact source_identity SHA map already sealed in M1830. The Formality Tcl later resolves those rows against the live hw_autoresearch_nts07 tree and reads them freshly.
findings.impact: An RTL file can drift after M1832/M1834/M1836 source sealing while preserving the filelist SHA. The future proof would then evaluate a different reference source identity. If the drift is formally equivalent, the run can still publish raw PASS, so equivalence alone does not restore exact provenance.
findings.required_fix: A superseding source identity must carry the exact 13 path-to-SHA map and the runner must verify every live RTL file immediately before attempt creation and again inside the sealed input identity. The independent source checker/tests must reject a one-file content drift.

findings.title: Future release cannot bind the M1834 review manifest and outer seal
findings.evidence: verify_authority() obtains M1834 review/manifest/outer digests from caller environment and validates the directory, but expected_identity for M1836 contains only m1834_source_review_sha256. Because the release identity is compared for exact dictionary equality, M1836 cannot add manifest or outer-seal pins without being rejected.
findings.impact: The launch release is not the complete authority for the exact independently sealed review population. Caller-supplied manifest/outer values can be selected outside the release, creating an authority-role bypass even though review.json itself is pinned.
findings.required_fix: A superseding runner/release schema must require and exact-compare m1834_source_review_manifest_sha256 and m1834_source_review_outer_seal_file_sha256 inside the release identity, with negative tests for removal, swap and caller-only substitution.

findings.title: Raw PT verification does not require or semantically adjudicate the full promised report set
findings.evidence: verify_pt() requires check_timing, analysis_coverage, global_timing, setup, hold, constraints, clock, libraries, runtime scope and machine summary, but not exceptions.rpt, design.rpt or wire_load.rpt despite the contract/Tcl promising them. It parses only finite setup/hold slack; check_timing, coverage and constraint reports are not semantically gated.
findings.impact: The raw result remains pending independent review, so this is not an authorization blocker if the result hammer requires all reports and adjudicates unconstrained/untested/violator counts. It must not be silently promoted from raw PASS.
findings.required_fix: The superseding source should preferably require all emitted reports. At minimum, the post-run independent result hammer must reject missing/empty exceptions, design or wire-load reports and report nonzero unconstrained, untested or constraint-violation counts without hiding negative slack.

required_next_gate: Author a new superseding source identity that exact-pins and runtime-verifies all 13 live RTL sources and makes the future release bind the complete independent review seal triplet. It must receive a different-author severity-zero source hammer before any EDA or release.
